description: A quantile reads the time that nine in ten responses stay within
code:
times = [120, 80, 300, 95, 110, 140]
p90 = times.quantile(0.9)
assert(p90, 220)
times.push(250)
p90

description: The quartiles of a list are its 0.25 and 0.75 quantiles
code:
prices = [12, 7, 3, 25, 9]
low = prices.quantile(0.25)
high = prices.quantile(0.75)
assert([low, high], [7, 12])
prices.push(40)
[low, high]

description: The 0.5 quantile of a list is its median
A selector takes a quantile of a property over a class population
code:
class Parcel(weight):
    this.weight = weight
Parcel(3)
Parcel(5)
heavy = Parcel(10)
upper = Parcel.quantile(0.75, parcel -> parcel.weight)
assert(upper, 7.5)
heavy.weight = 4
upper

description: A quantile over a filtered population follows each new instance
code:
class Trip(city, minutes):
    this.city = city
    this.minutes = minutes
Trip("oslo", 30)
Trip("oslo", 34)
Trip("bergen", 90)
slow = Trip.filter(trip -> trip.city == "oslo").quantile(0.5, trip -> trip.minutes)
assert(slow, 32)
Trip("oslo", 50)
slow

description: A rank held in a variable is followed when it changes
code:
rank = 0.25
levels = [4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]
q = levels.quantile(rank)
assert(q, 9.75)
rank = 0.75
q

description: A single value is every quantile of itself, and an empty list gives NaN
code:
samples = [7]
q = samples.quantile(0.3)
assert(q, 7)
samples.pop()
String(q)

description: Two equal neighbours give their own value
code:
levels = [3, 3, 9]
q = levels.quantile(0.01)
assert(q, 3)
levels.push(1)
q

description: A class-level rule keeps the 0.75 quantile of each sensor's readings
code:
class Sensor(readings):
    this.readings = readings
$Sensor.peak = $Sensor.readings.quantile(0.75)
hall = Sensor([18, 21, 19, 24])
assert(hall.peak, 21.75)
hall.readings.push(30)
hall.peak

description: A rank outside 0 to 1 raises a typed error
code:
xs = [1, 2]
failure = ""
try:
    xs.quantile(90)
catch error:
    failure = error
failure
return: "TypeError: quantile expects a number from 0 to 1"

description: A failed selector rolls back the change that triggered it
code:
def checked(level):
    if level < 0:
        throw "NEGATIVE"
    return level
levels = [3, 5, 10]
high = levels.quantile(0.75, checked)
try:
    levels.push(-1)
catch error:
    pass
[levels.length, high]

description: A function named quantile keeps its meaning beside the query
code:
def quantile(values, q) => values.length * q
xs = [1, 3]
[quantile(xs, 0.5), xs.quantile(0.5)]
